correctness.rationale: C PASS. For integers u≥3 and even n≥4, the recurrence has strong divisibility gcd(U_i,U_j)=U_gcd(i,j), a primitive minimal triple, gcd(a,b)=u, and identity (u²−1)b=a+u c. At n=4 and 6|n the Apéry normal-form reductions provide distinct residues and a rectangular Apéry set, yielding two binomial toric relations, symmetric Frobenius formulas and Hilbert series. For other even n≥8 (3∤n), the only possible gcd gluing is (a,b) and forces c=x(a/u)+y(b/u); gcd(A,B)=1 then A|d−y with 1≤d−y≤d<A, impossible. The Herzog three-generator criterion applies; finite Apéry checks are supplementary, not proof.

evidence: Thus the necessary equivalence in recurrence hypotheses is absent; a classical gluing theorem does not imply that n=4 or 6|n without new number-theoretic gcd analysis.
